page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 architecture using the AWS Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the average tier, multi-core execution is highly efficient, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory subsystem performance is exceptionally strong, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 11,082.32 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 481.61 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 10%, with Redis handling 198.49 million operations per second.

The server exhibits specific performance tradeoffs. While LLM text generation for medium and large models ranks in the top tier, prompt processing speeds for those same models remain in the average tier, and text generation for small models falls into the bottom 25%. Given the absence of local storage and GPUs, this server is designed for memory-intensive, network-bound workloads. The high memory density and strong multi-core throughput make it suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed memory-intensive data processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.24xlarge is an ARM64 memory-optimized server featuring 96 dedicated physical cores on the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core and memory subsystem performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 198.49 million operations per second and uncached memory read bandwidth at 481.61 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics and small-model LLM text generation show average to weak performance. This profile makes the instance highly efficient for memory-intensive, network-bound workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed caching, and high-throughput web serving, offering strong resource density for enterprise-scale memory requirements.
